title: Where does 0.6 × 0.7 land?
hook: Two decimals, one product. Does it land above them, between them, or below them?

doesNotKnow: that multiplying by a number below 1 gives a smaller result

objective: The learner can explain that 0.6 × 0.7 = 0.42 is smaller than both, because multiplying by 0.7 keeps seven tenths of the 0.6 strip, and that a product grows only when the other number is above 1.

claims.text: 0.6 × 0.7 = 0.42, which is smaller than 0.6 and smaller than 0.7.
claims.source: 60 × 70 = 4,200 ten-thousandths = 0.42. node: 6*7/100 = 0.42. The stage computes area in tenths, (6 × h10) / 100, so it prints 0.42 exactly. | FC pass 35 (fact-checker, 2026-10-14): VERIFIED. Own node: area(7) = 6*7/100 = 0.42 -> '0.42'; 0.42 < 0.6 and 0.42 < 0.7. Reveal prints num(area(KEY10)) with the 'seven' milestone required.

claims.text: The area of a rectangle 0.6 wide and h tall is 0.6 × h, also when the sides are not whole numbers (stage: the shaded rectangle and the 'Area' readout).
claims.source: Cut the rectangle into hundredth squares: 6 × 7 tenth-by-tenth squares of 1/100 each = 42/100. The stage draws the rectangle 0.6 × h units and labels it with area(h10). | FC pass 35 (fact-checker, 2026-10-14): VERIFIED. Derivation: for a rectangle of sides 0.6 and h (h = k/10), it is 6k cells of 0.1 x 0.1 = 0.01 each, area 6k/100 = 0.6h, the same rule as for whole sides. The shaded rect is (A10/10)U wide and (h10/10)U tall, so its drawn area is 0.6h of the unit square; the readout prints '0.6 × h = area' for all 21 slider values (own node, no float artefacts).

claims.text: Multiplying by 0.7 keeps seven tenths of the 0.6 strip, so it shrinks it.
claims.source: 0.6 × 0.7 is 7/10 of 0.6 × 1. On the stage the strip (0.6 × 1) is outlined and the shaded part at h = 0.7 covers 7 of its 10 tenth-rows. | FC pass 35 (fact-checker, 2026-10-14): VERIFIED. Derivation: 0.6 x 0.7 = 0.7 of 0.6 (seven of the strip's ten tenths), 0.42 < 0.6. On the stage the shaded part at h = 0.7 covers 7/10 of the dashed 0.6 strip's height.

claims.text: At height 1 the area stays 0.6, and above 1 (for example 0.6 × 1.5 = 0.9) it grows: for a positive number a, a × b is smaller than a when b < 1, equal when b = 1 and larger when b > 1.
claims.source: a·b − a = a(b − 1), which has the sign of b − 1 when a > 0. node: 0.6*0.5 = 0.3, 0.6*1 = 0.6, 0.6*1.5 = 0.9 (tenths arithmetic). The reveal quotes the largest h above 1 the learner set, from area(h10). | FC pass 35 (fact-checker, 2026-10-14): VERIFIED. Own node: area(10) = 0.6, area(15) = 0.9, and every h > 1 on the slider gives area > 0.6 (up to 1.2 at h = 2), so the reveal's 'at X, did it grow, to Y' is true for whichever largest h > 1 is recorded. General statement: a*b - a = a(b - 1), whose sign for a > 0 is the sign of b - 1.

recall.question: Without working it out exactly: is 8 × 0.9 more or less than 8?
recall.why: 0.9 is below 1, so 8 × 0.9 keeps nine tenths of 8 (7.2). Multiplying makes bigger only when the other number is above 1.
